ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast ratio defined by a dominant low-intensity (black) base covering approximately 85-90% of the visible surface, punctuated by high-intensity (white/light-grey) linear and circular pixel clusters.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: High-intensity pixel distributions are localized in two primary forms: terminal clusters at the distal tips of both lobes and a network of non-contiguous linear filaments (scars) dispersed across the medial and lateral regions of the black surface.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Sharp V-shaped vertex with a calculated angle of approximately 55 degrees, showing a vertical depth approximately 1/5th the height of the visible lobe.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations visible along the entire trailing boundary, with higher pixel-amplitude variations (jagged peaks) occurring toward the distal tips.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex trailing edge curve that tapers sharply toward the distal points, with the left lobe appearing slightly more rounded than the right lobe in the 2D plane.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Clearly defined clusters of white, roughly circular pixel groupings (barnacles) concentrated at the terminal distal points of both the left and right fluke lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Extensive network of multi-directional white linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) crossing the black pigment, particularly prominent on the lower interior section of the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Presence of multiple parallel vertical linear scars (rake marks) on the left lobe and significant biological encrustation at the fluke extremities.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique density of parallel scarring on the inner left lobe and asymmetrical wear on the trailing edge serrations.
